title: Ask
lead: Write it as you would tell a colleague. This is not an AI that answers. It asks one thing at a time and keeps what it heard on the right, in your words. When the starting point holds, you can send it to me.

doors.chat: Hand over a chat with an AI

chat_lead: Paste the conversation you already had with an AI about this. I read it for the same five lines; what it does not contain, I ask.
chat_placeholder: Paste the whole chat, your messages and the AI's answers.
heard_note: Mechanical reading, no model; nothing leaves this page until you send. Every line is your sentence. Click a line to change it.

turns.solution: “{q}” reads as a solution. I keep it under already decided. What happens now, and for whom? One observed fact is enough.
turns.method: A question about how I work is not a request; the task contract describes it. What is going on at your end?
turns.agent_alone: An agent asking on its own behalf is declined. Who is the person or organisation behind this?

ask.object: Where does this sit: the public site, the app people log into, the data, or how the organisation works?
ask.decision: What do you need to decide, or get moving, once this is clear?
ask.who: Who has this day to day, and who says yes to a change?
ask.current: What happens now, and for whom? One observed fact is enough.
ask.users_asked: Has anyone who uses it day to day been asked? What did they say?

ask_again.object: I still have no place for it. Is it the public site, the app, the data, or the organisation?
ask_again.decision: Still missing: what you will do once this is clear. One sentence.
ask_again.who: Still missing: who has this day to day, and who decides.
ask_again.current: Still missing: one thing that happens now. Not the wish, the fact.

turns.collected: That holds. Check the lines on the right; click one to change it. Then send.

contract_line: What a request and an answer look like: the task contract.

glossary.who: Who has the problem: the person who feels it day to day. Who decides: the one who says yes to a change.
glossary.object: Where it sits: the thing the problem lives in. The public website is the site anyone can open; the app is what people log into; data is what is measured; the organisation is who owns and decides.
glossary.current: What happens now: one observed fact, in your words. Not what you want, what you see.
glossary.decision: The decision this informs: what you will do differently once this is clear, and by when.
glossary.decided: Already decided or fixed: what is not up for discussion, including a solution that was already chosen.
glossary.users_asked: The people who use it day to day: whether they have been asked, and what they said.
glossary.lens: My lens: the way I read a problem. I find the underlying problem before you build the wrong solution. The task contract describes it.
glossary.collected: Collected means the four required lines are there, in your words. It is a starting point, not a judgement; the judgement comes after you send and pay.

glossary_fallback: I only ask and keep what you say; I do not answer questions here. The task contract describes what I do. Where were we:
collected_label: Collected: a starting point for my lens.
